user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
## Benefits of Code Review for Small Teams

- **Catches bugs early** – Issues found before merging are cheaper to fix
- **Knowledge sharing** – Team members learn each other's approaches and spread domain knowledge
- **Consistency** – Enforces coding standards and keeps the codebase uniform
- **Reduces bus factor** – No single person is the only one who understands a section of code
- **Mentorship** – Junior developers get direct, contextual feedback
- **Better design** – A second set of eyes often surfaces simpler or more maintainable solutions
- **Accountability** – Developers write more carefully knowing others will read their code

**Bottom line:** For small teams, code review is one of the highest-ROI practices — it improves quality while doubling as documentation, training, and team alignment.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain a consistent, high-quality codebase.

1. **Bug detection** – Errors are caught before merging, reducing costly fixes later.
2. **Knowledge sharing** – Team members learn from each other's code, reducing reliance on any single person.
Code review builds a **culture of accountability and collaboration**, encouraging developers to write more thoughtfully knowing their peers will read their work.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: Knowledge silos can form, leaving critical parts of the codebase understood by only one person — a serious risk if that person leaves the team.
Track **defect escape rate** — the number of bugs found in production versus those caught during review — to measure how effectively code reviews are improving quality.
Code review is a small investment that pays dividends in quality, collaboration, and long-term team resilience.

• Small investment, big returns in code quality
• Strengthens team collaboration and shared ownership
• Builds a more resilient, maintainable codebase over time
Code review is essential for small teams to ship better code, share knowledge, and stay resilient.
Code review is only effective if feedback is timely and constructive — slow or overly critical reviews can bottleneck progress and harm team morale.
Done well, code review improves quality; done poorly, it hinders.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only when done consistently and constructively.
